A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NAG test is a reliable method for predicting ARD, especially if the test is performed in a way that takes the slower-reacting minerals into account.
the mineralogy-based method is the most promising method for ARD prediction.

the static laboratory tests and mineralogical calculations give comparable results, but the mineralogical calculations have the potential to be more accurate, especially in the case of slow-reacting silicates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mineralogy of the mine waste is a key factor that should be taken into account in ARD prediction.
mineralogical calculations should be used in addition to static tests, especially when the results of these tests are inconclusive.
ARD prediction methods should be adapted to the specific characteristics of the site in question, and the use of static laboratory methods should be complemented with mineralogical calculations.
